In Kinnula, 164 km by road from Jyväskylä, 15 breast sessions mean 16 nights away versus 6 with 5 [S60, S59].

1. The head of radiotherapy could evaluate a single 8 Gy session as default for uncomplicated painful bone metastases (equal pain relief, more retreatment), serving "National targets and key effectiveness indicators defined for agreed cancers" [S31, S30, S62, S61]. In Kinnula, expected nights away are 6.2 with multi-fraction versus 2.4 with a single 8 Gy session [S60, S30]. Within 30 days, the clinical team reviews which cases qualify [S31, S62].

2. The breast lead could evaluate 5 sessions as default for eligible patients (whole breast or chest wall without nodal radiotherapy), naming distance as a reason, as it is non-inferior, serving "Patients receive treatment within target times" [S9, S11, S15, S14, S25, S24]. Yearly county-wide, this removes 71 nights away and frees 850 machine sessions (calculated, breast) [S33, S57, S34, S35, S60]. Within 30 days, the clinical team reviews eligibility and distance criteria [S15, S14].

3. The quality manager could report schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band yearly, serving "Regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services (cross-cutting indicator)" [S21, S27, S26]. Within 30 days, the quality manager and the clinical team decide which figures to report [S21, S27].

Distances use municipality centre points and the current schedule mix is unknown [S59, S60, S57].
